answer: Anchor every agent identity to a hardware kernel: the host's trusted kernel signs one identity key, bound to a single physical machine, and the network only accepts identities whose kernel signature chains to a known hardware root. A sybil farmer cannot mint thousands of fake agents in software — each extra identity costs a real device and a key ceremony. Trust then grows glacier-slow: new identities start weightless and earn weight only through months of attested useful work, so a flood of fresh clones arrives with zero influence and the cost of forging a credible army dwarfs any reward.
